resources.string: Install or remove the OpenCode coding agent in Termux — native build, no proot.
Termux is not installed. Install it first; this app only handles setup.
Runs opencode --version in Termux and prints what it answers. Nothing is installed, removed or changed.

Setup runs inside Termux in the background, so this screen stays in front, and every command streams its output on the page that started it.
You may need Termux\'s \"allow external apps\" setting for this app to send commands: add allow-external-apps=true to ~/.termux/termux.properties.

Termux will add a signed APT repository and install:
• the opencode package (~70 MB download, ~209 MB installed) — a native Android/aarch64 build from the third-party project bd-loser/opencode-bionic, since upstream ships glibc-only binaries that cannot run in Termux, • nothing else: no proot, no glibc runtime, no npm.
The command, run in Termux:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MBanucu/opencode-termux-setup/main/install.sh | bash
Nothing is uploaded. Use Wi-Fi if mobile data is metered. You can cancel now and run the same step by hand later.
This removes the opencode package and the APT repository that the installer added. Choose what happens to your data.
Your provider credentials, sessions and settings in ~/.config/opencode and ~/.local/share/opencode are kept, so installing again picks up where you left off.
Also deletes those two directories: provider credentials, sessions and settings. Every provider has to be connected again, and sessions cannot be recovered.

Termux only accepts commands from other apps when this is enabled in its own settings:
allow-external-apps=true
Add that line to ~/.termux/termux.properties inside Termux, then run termux-reload-settings (or restart Termux), and try again. The command is copied to the clipboard for you.
This app hands exactly one command to Termux, and Termux only accepts it with its RUN_COMMAND permission granted. Android asked for it and the request was declined.
This app does not install opencode by itself: it starts the install in Termux. Install Termux from F-Droid, then come back.
